'''Chemence''' is a speciality chemical and medical device manufacturer which products include [[cyanoacrylate]] adhesives,<ref>{{cite book |last=Dillard |first=David |date=2010 |title= Advances in Structural Adhesive Bonding |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5YdwAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA124 |publisher=Elsevier |pages=124–6 |isbn=978-1845698058
}}</ref> anaerobic adhesives,<ref>{{cite web|work = Adhesive Magazine |title = Our seventh annual listing of the country's top manufacturers of adhesives/sealants; pressure sensitives; and adhesive/sealants products. |url = http://www.adhesivesmag.com/articles/84337-asi-50}}</ref> impregnation [[sealant]]s,<ref>{{cite book |last=Dunn |first=David |date=2003 |title= Adhesives and Sealants: Technology, Applications and Markets |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ky8QH02d7zkC&pg=PA136 |publisher=iSmithers Rapra Publishing |page=136 |isbn=1859573657
}}</ref> adhesive activators,<ref>{{cite book |last=Grillone |first=Gregory A.  |date=2014 |title= Robotic Surgery of the Head and Neck|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9m53BQAAQBAJ&pg=PA128 |publisher=Springer |page=128 |isbn=978-1493915477
}}</ref> [[epoxy resins]],<ref>{{cite book |last=Dunn |first=David |date=2003 |title= Adhesives and Sealants: Technology, Applications and Markets |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ky8QH02d7zkC&pg=PA136 |publisher=iSmithers Rapra Publishing |page=136 |isbn=1859573657
}}</ref> UV adhesives, [[photopolymer]] resins,<ref>{{cite web|work = Flexography |title = Chemence to Open Technology Center |url = https://www.flexography.org/industry-news/chemence-to-open-technology-center/|date = 9 April 2013 }}</ref> custom [[printer (computing)|printer]] [[ink cartridge]]s, [[Gas pipe]] sealants,<ref>{{cite book |last=  |first=   |date=2002 |title= International Gas Engineering and Management, Volume 42|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=K1dWAAAAMAAJ&q=chemence|publisher=Institution of Gas Engineers |page=  |isbn=
}}</ref> and soak off [[nail polish]]es.<ref>{{cite web|work = Yahoo Finance |title =Chemence Medical Receives FDA Clearance for Exofin® Tissue Adhesive |url = https://finance.yahoo.com/news/chemence-medical-receives-fda-clearance-130000636.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work = IGEM |title =Chemence |url = http://www.igem.org.uk/about-igem/directory/affiliates-directory/chemence-ltd.aspx}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Cameron  |first= John  |date=2013 |title= Current Surgical Therapy|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QwYyAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA657|publisher=Saunders; 11 edition |page= 657  |isbn=978-1455740079
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work = Bloomberg |title =Chemence |url = https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=6872228}}</ref> Chemence is a supplier of [[photopolymer]] and commercial printers to the [[flexographic]] industry in the US and Europe,<ref>{{cite book |last=Dunn |first=David |date=2003 |title= Adhesives and Sealants: Technology, Applications and Markets |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ky8QH02d7zkC&pg=PA136 |publisher=iSmithers Rapra Publishing |page=136 |isbn=1859573657
}}</ref> as well as the primary sealant supplier to [[British Gas]],<ref>{{cite book |last=  |first=  |date=1997 |title= Gas Engineering and Management, Volume 37|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zlVWAAAAMAAJ&q=chemence|publisher=Institution of Gas Engineers |page=  |isbn= 
}}</ref> and a primary supplier of private-label adhesives to companies including [[Tesco]], [[3M]], [[Bostik]], and [[Bondo (putty)|Bondo]].<ref>{{cite web|work = 3M |title =3M Acquires Industrial Adhesives Product Line from Chemence Inc. |url = http://news.3m.com/press-release/company/3m-acquires-industrial-adhesives-product-line-chemence-inc}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|journal =   Pigment & Resin Technology|volume =36 |issue =3 |title =3M acquires industrial adhesives product line from Chemence Inc. |doi =10.1108/prt.2007.12936cab.006 |year =2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work = Chemicals Technology |title =Chemence denies FTC charges over 'Made in the USA' dispute |url = http://www.chemicals-technology.com/news/newschemence-denies-ftc-charges-over-made-in-the-usa-dispute-4805060|date =8 February 2016 }}</ref> The company's catalogue of patents includes processes, [[packaging]] devices, and [[chemical]] combinations.<ref>{{cite web|work = Justia Patents |title = Patents by Assignee Chemence, Inc. |url = http://patents.justia.com/assignee/chemence-inc}}</ref>

==History==
Chemence was founded in London, England, in 1983 by Hugh V. Cooke.<ref>{{cite web|work = Bloomberg |title =Company Overview of Chemence Limited |url = https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=171357782}}</ref> The company originally traded under the name Lockshield Ltd., which in 1985 was changed to Chemence Ltd. The firm initially specialised in manufacturing industrial [[adhesive]]s and [[sealants]], developing a method for sealing [[cast iron]] gas joints for [[British Gas]] using anaerobic sealants under 'live' conditions.<ref>{{cite web|work = Companies House |title = Chemence Limited |url = https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/01746313}}</ref> This allowed further development of a range of anaerobic sealants for a number of industrial practices.<ref>{{cite book |last=Dunn |first=David |date=2003 |title= Adhesives and Sealants: Technology, Applications and Markets |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ky8QH02d7zkC&pg=PA136 |publisher=iSmithers Rapra Publishing |page=134 |isbn=1859573657
}}</ref>

In 1986, Chemence Ltd. acquired the assets of Alembic Chemicals, a [[cyanoacrylate]] manufacturer in [[Dublin]], Ireland.  In 1988, the facility was moved to [[Corby]] (England), expanding product development and manufacturing to encompass anaerobic thread lockers ([[thread-locking fluid]]), retaining compounds, gasket makers and pipe sealants, [[UV]] curing products, and cyanoacrylate adhesives for consumer and industrial markets.<ref>{{cite web|work = Companies UK |title = Chemence Ltd. |url = https://www.companiesintheuk.co.uk/ltd/chemence}}</ref> Chemence Ltd. also manufactured a range of private label consumer adhesives for companies including [[Bostik]], [[ASDA]], [[TESCO]], and [[B&Q]].<ref>{{cite web|work = Chemence |title = Chemence story |url = http://www.chemence.com/our-company/chemence-story/}}</ref>

In 1989, the company opened a distribution office in [[Cleveland]], Ohio, under the name Chemence Inc.<ref>{{cite web|work = Bloomberg |title = Company Overview of Chemence Inc. |url = https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=6872228/}}</ref> In 1993, Chemence Inc. relocated to [[Alpharetta, Georgia]], and became the only manufacturer of [[cyanoacrylates]] adhesives and sealants in the US.<ref>{{cite book |last=  |first=  |date=2003 |title= Medical Polymers|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Msraj84oBWMC&pg=PA129|publisher=iSmithers Rapra Publishing |page= 129  |isbn= 1859573355
}}</ref> Subsequently, [[Cordis (medical)]] commissioned Chemence Inc. to develop a liquid [[embolic]] used for the treatment of AVM ([[arteriovenous malformations]]).<ref>{{cite web|work = Business Wire |title =Micrus Endovascular and Chemence Medical Products Sign Development Agreement for Liquid Embolic Products |url =  http://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20080423005393/en/Micrus-Endovascular-Chemence-Medical-Products-Sign-Development|date =23 April 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work =Biz Journals |title =Micrus, Chemence in development agreement |url =  http://www.bizjournals.com/sanjose/stories/2008/04/21/daily42.html}}</ref> This led to the founding of Chemence Medical Inc. in 1994.<ref>{{cite web|work =Business Wire |title =Chemence Medical Receives FDA Clearance for Exofin® Tissue Adhesive |url =  http://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20160215005097/en/Chemence-Medical-Receives-FDA-Clearance-Exofin%C2%AE-Tissue|date =15 February 2016 }}</ref> Chemence Medical Inc. specialised in cyanoacrylate (CA)-based medical devices.<ref>{{cite web |work =Reuters |title =Octylseal Supply Agreement between Chemence Medical Products, Inc. and Medline Industries, Inc. Has Terminated |url =https://www.reuters.com/article/ga-chemence-medical-prod-idUSnBw30Dd73a+110+BSW20130326 }}{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher =NASDAQ |title =Micrus Endovascular Corporation (MEND) Presentation |url = http://www.nasdaq.com/aspx/call-transcript.aspx?StoryID=78530&Title=micrus-endovascular-q4-2008-earnings-call-transcript}}</ref> Its first product for [[Cordis (medical)]] was TruFill liquid embolic.<ref>{{cite web|work =FDA |title =TRUFILL® n-Butyl Cyanoacrylate (n-BCA) Liquid Embolic System |url = https://www.fda.gov/MedicalDevices/ProductsandMedicalProcedures/DeviceApprovalsandClearances/Recently-ApprovedDevices/ucm089765.htm|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090709233920/http://www.fda.gov/MedicalDevices/ProductsandMedicalProcedures/DeviceApprovalsandClearances/Recently-ApprovedDevices/ucm089765.htm|url-status = dead|archive-date = 9 July 2009}}</ref> In 1994, the company developed and patented a variant of [[superglue]] used to repair inoperable [[aneurysm]]s in the brain. Subsequently, Chemence Medical became a retailer of [[Dentistry|dental]], [[topical]] [[tissue (biology)|tissue]], and [[veterinary]] adhesives to medical device companies in the US.

In 2000, Chemence Inc. and Chemence Ltd. began manufacturing [[photopolymer]] and resins, supplying to international [[corrugated galvanised iron|corrugated]], printing, and [[Packaging and labeling|packing]] industries.<ref>{{cite book |last=  |first=  |date=2003 |title= Medical Polymers|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Msraj84oBWMC&q=chemence&pg=PA129|publisher=iSmithers Rapra Publishing |page= 129  |isbn= 1859573355
}}</ref> In 2001, Chemence Medical developed a consumer liquid [[bandage]] for [[3M]], marketed under the Nexcare brand.<ref>{{cite web|title =Pattents |url = https://patents.google.com/patent/US20080075862}}</ref> In 2005, Chemence Medical began manufacturing its own line of [[FDA]]-registered medical device products including Liquid Skin skin protectant, Derma+Flex liquid bandage, Derma+Flex gel tissue adhesive (CE marked), Salon Safe liquid bandage, Sure Close wound closure kit, Derma+flex QS gel tissue adhesive, Gluture veterinary glue, Exofin tissue adhesive, Exofin micro and Exofin Fusion skin closure system.<ref>{{cite web|work =Chemence Medical|title =Products |url = http://chemencemedical.com/}}</ref>

In 2007, the company negotiated the sale of the intellectual property rights for the RITE-LOK range of industrial adhesives and sealants to [[3M]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher =Manufacturing.net|title =3M Acquiring Chemence's Industrial Adhesives Product Linet |url = http://www.manufacturing.net/news/2007/02/3m-acquiring-chemences-industrial-adhesives-product-line|date =February 2007 }}</ref> In 2011, [[3M]] rebranded the RITE-LOK product range to Scotch-Weld.<ref>{{cite web|work =3M|title =RITE-LOK™ Rebranded! |url = http://solutions.3m.com/wps/portal/3M/en_EU/Industrial-Adhesives-Tapes/-/News/?PC_Z7_RJH9U52300FJD0I1LVGPHG2CD1000000_assetId=1273687467808}}</ref> In 2012, Chemence Ltd. re-launched their own range of industrial adhesives and sealants under the Krylex brand name.<ref>{{cite web|work =Chemence|title =Krylex|url =http://www.chemence.com/products-services/krylex/|access-date =13 May 2016|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20160502052507/http://www.chemence.com/products-services/krylex/|archive-date =2 May 2016|url-status =dead}}</ref> In 2014, the [[Flexographic]] Division of Chemence Inc. developed the Genesys Platemaking System, a process in liquid platemaking that allowed faster and more cost-efficient manufacturing.<ref>{{cite web|work =Chemence|title =Products|url =http://www.chemence.com/products-services/graphics/#genesys-product }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title =Patents|url =https://patents.google.com/patent/US20140162192 }}</ref> In the same year, Chemence acquired a number of printing and platemaking companies in Great Britain and Spain to form Chemence Graphics, which became one of the largest printing service providers in Europe.{{citation needed|date=May 2016}}

In 2015, Chemence Graphics created a proprietary plate for [[Smurfit Kappa]], and expanded platemaking facilities to France and Germany.<ref>{{cite web|work =Chemence|title =Smurfit Kappa Case Study|url =http://www.chemence.com/science-sustainability/|access-date =13 May 2016|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20160502053101/http://www.chemence.com/science-sustainability/|archive-date =2 May 2016|url-status =dead}}</ref> Also in 2015, the company began manufacturing Krylex, its own formulation based on RITE-LOK, which was purchased by [[3M]].<ref>{{cite web|work =3M|title =3M Acquires Industrial Adhesives Product Line from Chemence Inc.|url =http://news.3m.com/es/press-release/company/3m-acquires-industrial-adhesives-product-line-chemence-inc }}</ref> In 2016, [[DVGW]] (Deutsche Vereinigung des Gas und Wasserfaches) accredited Chemence Ltd. for its anaerobic gas pipe sealant Krylex KS775. The [[DVGW]] accreditation approved the use of Chemence product Krylex KS775 for municipalities providing gas and water services across Europe.<ref>{{cite web|work =Chemence|title =Krylex® KS775 Has Received DVGW Certification|url =http://www.chemence.com/ks775-has-received-dvgw-certification/|access-date =13 May 2016|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20160419024505/http://www.chemence.com/ks775-has-received-dvgw-certification/|archive-date =19 April 2016|url-status =dead}}</ref>

extract: Chemence is a speciality chemical and medical device manufacturer which products include cyanoacrylate adhesives, anaerobic adhesives, impregnation sealants, adhesive activators, epoxy resins, UV adhesives, photopolymer resins, custom printer ink cartridges, Gas pipe sealants, and soak off nail polishes. Chemence is a supplier of photopolymer and commercial printers to the flexographic industry in the US and Europe, as well as the primary sealant supplier to British Gas, and a primary supplier of private-label adhesives to companies including Tesco, 3M, Bostik, and Bondo. The company's catalogue of patents includes processes, packaging devices, and chemical combinations.
